findings.scenario: A production deployment runs after the Railway service migration while the Dockerfile cache mount and railway-deploy.yml still carry retired project/service identifiers, so Railway rejects the Dockerfile at BUILD_IMAGE validation
findings.invariant: The Dockerfile cache mount uses the live production service id in Railway's documented service-scoped form, and the manual Railway workflow targets the live production project, environment, and service
findings.note: The configuration correction is implemented in this PR, but production verification remains pending. The repository workflow is intentionally workflow_dispatch-only: merging to main does not deploy. After merge, issue #845 requires the owner to dispatch Railway Deploy from main, verify that the correct production service reaches terminal SUCCESS, and complete the agreed smoke check. Native Railway autodeploy is not assumed or claimed; Railway documents that it requires a project member with a connected GitHub account and contributor access. Rollback, if required, is through the Railway Deployments menu to the previous successful deployment, subject to image-retention limits.
